The section is a cohesive contract-penalty rule for highway construction or maintenance contracts involving the Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Penalty clauses in Minister highway contracts
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections identify when contract penalties may be used, how penalties are measured, and that penalty amounts may be withheld from Crown payments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how penalty clauses may operate in Minister highway construction or maintenance contracts.

reason: The section is a focused rule for removing buildings from a highway right-of-way, including notice, removal methods, and compensation limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Removing buildings from a highway right-of-way
proposedGroups.reason: All subsections address Ministerial removal of buildings from the highway right-of-way after notice, how removal may occur, and when compensation under section 24 is barred.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe the notice, removal methods, and compensation limit for buildings in a highway right-of-way.

reason: Section 65 contains distinct control-line topics: the designated line and construction prohibition, continuing offence consequences, Ministerial closure power, and permit records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Control line distance and construction prohibition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 65(2) to 65(4) set the maximum control-line distance, prohibit structures and driveways inside the line, and preserve existing objects between the highway center line and control line.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how a control line limits construction or placement near an arterial or collector highway.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Control line offences, closure power, and entrance permits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 65(5) to 65(8) address continuing offence fines, Ministerial closure of unlawful access, permits for entrance ways, permit cancellation, and public permit records.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the enforcement, closure, permit, and record rules tied to control line violations.

reason: The target states one rule preserving Crown vesting and Highway Act treatment for public roads omitted from a designation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Omitted public roads remain Crown roads dealt with as highways

evidenceText: Any public road not included in a designation under section 15

proposedGroups.reason: The section addresses public roads left out of a designation by error, omission, or bypass and states they remain vested in the Crown and may be dealt with as highways.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the effect when a public road is omitted from a highway designation by error, omission, or bypass.

reason: The target is a focused delegation rule for powers, rights, duties, or responsibilities relating to highways under the administration and control of the New Brunswick Highway Corporation or a project company.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Delegating highway powers for Corporation or project company highways
proposedGroups.reason: The subsection explains who may receive delegated highway authority and what a regulation may establish about direction, limits, terms, conditions, and sub-delegation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how highway-related powers may be delegated for highways administered by the New Brunswick Highway Corporation or a project company.

reason: Section 67 combines a broad list of regulation-making subjects with separate land-registration and effectiveness rules for controlled access highway and control line regulations.

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 67(1) lists the subjects the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may regulate, including permits, penalties, weighing, controlled access highways, utilities, highway use, maintenance, control lines, forms, and transitional matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the main Highway Act subjects that may be governed by regulation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration and effect of controlled access and control line regulations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 67(2) to 67(9) set the plan or description requirements, registration, commencement, website notice, and validity rules for controlled access highway and control line regulations.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how controlled access highway and control line regulations are described, registered, take effect, and remain valid despite notice failures.

reason: The section states which acquired lands constitute a highway for purposes of the Act, including land linked to usage agreements, permits, leases, and licences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land acquired for highway purposes constituting highway

evidenceText: Lands that are acquired under this Act or under the New Brunswick Highway Corporation Act
constitute a highway for the purposes of this Act

proposedGroups.reason: The target gives a single legal classification rule for lands acquired for highway purposes, with exceptions for portions outside the right-of-way and conflicting contexts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State when land acquired for highway purposes constitutes a highway under the Act.

reason: Section 69 separates listed highway offences from the special vehicle-owner liability and charging rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Listed highway obstruction and damage offences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 69(1) lists offence conduct involving encumbrances, water obstructions, altering highways or drains, disturbing ditch soil, damaging shoulders, traffic control devices, highways, bridges, culverts, and obstructing the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the highway obstruction, alteration, damage, and interference conduct made an offence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Vehicle owner liability and charging for weight violations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 69(2) and 69(3) address when a vehicle owner is deemed guilty of weight-related violations and how the owner may be charged.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how owner liability and charging work for vehicle weight violations.

reason: The section is a focused offence-classification provision for regulatory violations and Act provisions listed in Schedule A.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulation violations and Schedule A offence categories
proposedGroups.reason: The three subsections make regulatory non-compliance an offence, make Schedule A listed provisions offences, and tie those listed offences to Provincial Offences Procedure Act categories.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how section 70 creates offences and links Schedule A provisions to offence categories.

reason: The target lists the situations in which the Minister is not liable in nuisance for specified water, system, highway alteration, and ditch or drain conditions.

evidenceText: The Minister shall not be liable in an action in nuisance
water overflowing from a water or wastewater system

proposedGroups.reason: The section provides a single immunity rule for nuisance claims where damage results from listed highway, water, wastewater, storm water, ditch, drain, or watercourse conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the listed causes of damage for which the Minister has nuisance-liability immunity.

Schedule A is an authoritative table mapping Highway Act provisions to Provincial Offences Procedure Act offence categories.

proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Use Schedule A to match listed Highway Act offences with their category of offence.
